Singapore Civic District Tree Trail
tags.name: Yellow Flame (Peltophorum pterocarpum)

tags.description: The venerable Bodhi Tree was conserved during the site’s development – it was protected in place during construction and integrated into the Campus Green landscape.
tags.name: Bodhi Tree (Ficus religiosa)

tags.description: The Yellow Flame Tree (Peltophorum pterocarpum), planted along this stretch of Orchard Road, is a common wayside tree that produces brilliant yellow flowers.
tags.name: Yellow Flame Tree (Peltophorum pterocarpum)

tags.description: Red Flame (Delonix regia) is a fast-growing tree with large red flowers. The fruit is a long flattened green pid which turns black when ripe.
tags.name: Red Flame (Delonix regia)

tags.description: Traveller’s Palm is a symbol of the Raffles Hotel. It is believed that in the past, the Traveller’s Palm was a welcome sight to thirsty travellers, who could drink the rainwater collected in the base of the leaves.
tags.name: Traveller’s Palm (Ravenala madagascariensis)

tags.description: Golden Shower Tree (Cassia fistula), which produces clusters of long, hanging, bright yellow and fragrant flowers. Nearly all parts of the tree have medicinal properties.
tags.name: Golden Shower Tree (Cassia fistula)

tags.description: Here, you can find a majestic Rain Tree estimated to be over 80 years old! It was conserved and transplanted into this location during the development of SMU. At the time of transplanting, it stood 21 m in height,  had a 25 m canopy, and weighted 37 t.
tags.name: Rain Tree (Samanea saman)

tags.description: The tree is native to tropical Africa and was introduced to Singapore in the late 1970s and can grow up to 60 m in its native environment.
tags.name: East African Mahogany (Khaya nyasica)

tags.description: This popular ornamental tree was first introduced to Singapore in 1982 and is fast growing, requiring minimal maintenance. Its attractive yellow flowers attract butterflies, bees and birds.
tags.name: Golden Penda (Xanthostemon chrysanthus)

tags.description: Along Queen Street are beautiful Trumpet Trees that bloom in pink, mauve or white. Trumpet Trees can grow up to more than 30 m tall and  usually flower in April and August, after a prolonged dry spell.
tags.name: Trumpet Tree (Tabebuia rosea)

tags.description: Trumpet Tree (Tabebuia rosea) gets its common name from its large trumpet-shaped flowers. Although not related to Japan’s famous cherry blossom trees, it is sometimes referred to as ‘Singapore’s Sakura’.
The Angsana is widely distributed in Southeast Asia, where it grows naturally on flat coastal plains behind mangrove swamps or along inland rivers in forests where the dry season is not pronounced.
tags.name: Angsana

tags.description: Diospyros buxifolia, a native evergreen tree that can grow up to 30 m tall.
tags.name: Diospyros buxifolia

tags.description: These trees produce white, showy flowers and fruits that are eaten by bats and birds.
tags.name: Sea Apple (Syzygium grande)

tags.description: Admire the interesting aerial roots that descend from the tree. This tree has been endorsed as a Heritage Tree, as it can be seen in photographs taken in 1955 - evidence that it is more than 60 years old!
tags.name: Indian Rubber Tree (Ficus elastica)

tags.description: The common name is derived from the distinctive smooth trunk which is light grey to whitish-yellow and mottled with brown spots, resembling the hide of a leopard. The tree also produces clusters of bright yellow flowers.
tags.name: Leopard Tree (Libidibia ferrea)

tags.description: Common Red-stem Fig (Ficus variegata) has fruits (figs) that are borne in clusters along the trunk and main branches.
tags.name: Common Red-stem Fig (Ficus variegata)

tags.description: Traditionally, different parts of this tree are used for medicinal purposes.
tags.name: Creamy Yellow Frangipanis (Plumeria rubra)

tags.description: Native to Singapore and other parts of the region, this evergreen tree can grow to more than 20 m tall. The flesh of the mature seeds is used to make belinjau crackers, a type of Indonesian snack. Roots are used in medicine aginst poisoning and malaria.
tags.name: Belinjau (Gnetum gnemon)

tags.description: Saga (Adenanthera pavonina) trees produce hard, red and shiny seeds which symbolise love and yearning in Chinese culture.
tags.name: Saga (Adenanthera pavonina)

tags.description: The palms already appeared in the background of many photographs taken during the first National Day Parade held at the Padang in 1966.
tags.name: Royal Palm (Roystonea regia)

tags.description: Bears its flowers and fruits on thick long stalks that grow directly from the tree trunk. The large, fleshy flowers are attractive and fragrant. Its fruits are round and hard, resembling cannon balls, hence its common name.
Brazilian Ironwood (Libidibia ferrea) originates from tropical America. It can grow up to 20 m. The bark patches resemble a leopard's hide, hence the other common name, Leopard Tree.
tags.name: Leopard Tree (Libidibia ferrea)

tags.description: Also called Jejawi. Native to India, South China, Indochina, Malaysia, Polynesia, tropical Australia.
tags.name: Malayan Banyan (Ficus microcarpa)

tags.description: This tree has been standing here for more than 70 years, and was endorsed as a Heritage Tree in 2008. The Tamarind is a slow growing tree that is widely cultivated for its sweet-sourish fruit pulp known as "asam".
tags.name: Tamarind (Tamarindus indica)

tags.description: The species is native to tropical America, and this particular cultivar can grow up to 12 m tall. It produces large white flowers with a yellow centre and waxy petals that form a funnel.
tags.name: Singapore White Frangipanis (Plumeria obtusa ‘Singapore White’)

tags.description: The Champaca tree is often planted around Hindu temples. Their flowers, bright orange or yellow, give off a strong fragrance.
tags.name: Champaca (Magnolia champaca)

tags.description: Teak is a termite resistant species and therefore its wood is used in construction and for outdoor furniture.
tags.name: Teak
